claim_summary: The 4-snap gap between New England's 71-snap playtime denominator and its 67 statistical offensive plays is fully accounted for by four offensive snaps that were run and then nullified by a live-ball penalty: the Jobe defensive pass interference on a Maye deep incompletion at 9:22 of the second quarter, a 4-yard Stevenson run wiped out by a Campbell illegal block at 1:48 of the third quarter, a 6-yard Stevenson run wiped out by a Campbell offensive holding at 5:45 of the fourth quarter, and a Maye incompletion wiped out by a Vera-Tucker ineligible-downfield penalty at 3:03 of the fourth quarter. Pre-snap dead-ball fouls and the two nullified punt-formation plays are excluded because no offensive snap occurred. The playtime denominator is offense-only, and Stevenson's 60 snaps and 85% are computed on the 71-snap base.
notes: source_locator: page 3 'Final Team Statistics' (67 offensive plays) and page 16 'Playtime Percentage' (71-snap offensive base), decomposed against the play-by-play on pages 8-14. Method: every 'No Play' penalty in the play-by-play was classified by possession and by whether the ball was snapped. Four NE-possession fouls nullified an executed offensive play (pages 9, 12, 14); the remaining NE-possession 'No Play' entries were pre-snap dead-ball fouls (Moses false start, page 11) or punt-formation plays (roughing the kicker and a delay of game, pages 11-12), none of which is an offensive snap. CROSS-CHECK: the same method applied to Seattle yields exactly 2 nullified offensive snaps (the Bradford offensive offside that wiped out a Barner 4th-and-1 conversion, and the illegal shift that wiped out a Lock touchdown to Kupp), matching Seattle's own 50-snap playtime base against its 48 statistical offensive plays. The reconciliation therefore holds independently on both sides of the same book. OFFENSE-ONLY CONFIRMED: page 16 carries separate Offense, Defense and Special Teams columns, and NE's 71-snap offensive base equals Seattle's 71-snap defensive base while NE's 50-snap defensive base equals Seattle's 50-snap offensive base. DENOMINATOR WARNING for any rate built on the 67-play base: Stevenson's 60 snaps are measured on the 71-snap base and already include any nullified snaps he was on the field for. He was the ball carrier on 2 of the 4 nullified plays, so at most 58 and at least 56 of his 60 snaps were statistical offensive plays, giving a share on the 67-play base of between 83.6% and 86.6%. It is NOT 60/67 = 90%; the book does not expose per-player participation on nullified snaps, so an exact share on the 67-play base is not derivable.
